text:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a weird errorbudget spike for GPU region-us-east-2 this morning. Burn rate jumped ~6x between 03:10-03:25 UTC. Anyone else seeing that in grafana? :thinking:

maya: I saw alerts pop for the saturation SLO. Traces show many short failures (cold starts?) and a few 503s from the model pool.

jonathan: Linking the panel I pulled: `dashboard -> infra/gpu/slo-overview` — the 95th latency worsened, but p50 stable. Looks like tail latency, not full outage.

lee: Could be noisy retries causing saturation. We recently increased max_retries in the routing layer for older models. If retries overlap, bursts can spike GPU utilization.

anika: Prom query I ran: ```
# approximate pct of requests with latency > 1s
sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{le+"1"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
```
Not perfect, but shows tail fraction up to 8% in that window for us-east-2.

sam: Thanks. Two parallel threads: (1) reduce alert noise and avoid consuming error budget from transient spikes, (2) fix root cause so burn doesn't repeat.

jonathan: For (1) we should tune the alert to count sustained burn. Current alert triggers on `increase(error_budget_used[5m]) > X` which is too sensitive. Suggest using a burn-rate window and `for: 10m` or `max_over_time` to ignore sub-5m blips. Example: ```yaml
expr: (increase(slo_errors_total[15m]) / increase(slo_total_requests[15m])) / slo_target > 4
for: 10m
```

maya: Also add a cooldown so we don't alert repeatedly while the oncall is already paging. Debounce at alertmanager level with `group_interval` and `repeat_interval` tweaks.

lee: For (2) quick mitigation: temporarily lower max_retries and reduce per-route concurrency for the affected model tiers to prevent head-of-line blocking. We can also enable a short-lived fallback to a cheaper model variant.

anika: Observability improvements: capture `retry_count` label on our request metrics (we currently strip it before export) and add a grafana panel for `rate(retry_count_total[5m])` by model. That will show if retries spiked.

sam: Good. Cost angle: increased scrape cardinality and very high resolution metrics in region-us-east-2 are also pushing prometheus CPU. We need to limit label explosion. Any relabel ideas?

jonathan: We should relabel some high-cardinality labels at scrape time for node-exporter and our exporter. e.g., drop `request_id` and compact `model_version` into `model_family` for metrics we use for SLOs: ```yaml
- action: replace
  source_labels: ["model_version"]
  regex: "(.*)-(v[0-9]+)"
  replacement: "$1"
  target_label: "model_family"
```

maya: Also use federation for long-term retention dashboards; keep 5m resolution in long-term store, 15s in short-term for active regions. That reduces remote storage costs.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1034. Assigned: lee. Priority: P2. Links: https://incident.redwood/INC-2026-1034

lee: Action items I'll take now: 1) reduce retries for model-tier B in us-east-2 (5m rollback window), 2) add `for: 10m` to burn alert rule and add a `max_over_time` guard, 3) add `retry_count` label to exporter.

anika: I'll update dashboards — add a tail-latency panel (p99/p999) and a retry rate overlay. Also adjust grafana alert thresholds to use `absent()` to avoid firing when metrics drop.

sam: I'll coordinate postmortem template and errorbudget accounting. We should mark this as a transient policy-triggered burn and not a sustained SLA violation if it doesn't reoccur.

jonathan: One more: check network egress queueing in us-east-2 — a noisy link at 03:12 showed spikes in TCP retransmits on node-exporter logs. Could be infra networking causing request latencies.

maya: I'll pull the node-exporter logs and NIC stats. If we confirm network micro-outage, we should route traffic to another AZ for a time-limited period.

lee: Will report back in ~30m with retries rollback and alert rule push.

sam: Thanks all — please add short notes to the incident. We'll reconvene if burn doesn't drop in 1h. :thumbsup:
